output:
  html_document:

params:
  run_plots: false
  data_dir: null
  output_dir: "../data/figures_individual"
  n: 1000
  models: [gaussian, poisson, logit, probit]
  lambda_settings: null
  histogram_bins: 30
  figure_types: [qq, hist_estimates, hist_errors]
  require_complete: true
  overwrite: false
  previews: true
---

Draw individual vector PDFs from saved results. Set `data_dir` to a native
result folder, set `run_plots: true`, then Knit. Paths are relative to this Rmd.
The default only loads the plotting functions and does not create figures.

Each component is separate, with dimensions read from the configuration:

- `qq`: normal and joint chi-square QQ plots; Theorem 2 shows **debiased results only**.
- `hist_estimates`: overlaid histograms of raw and debiased Lambda matrix entries.
- `hist_errors`: the same estimates after subtracting their true entries.

All labels use LaTeX (Latin Modern), including `$\Lambda^\star$`. QQ plots use
open circles and no confidence band. Histograms share bins, show density, and
use coral and blue. `pdflatex` with `lmodern` and Cairo-enabled R are required;
`pdftoppm` is optional for PNG previews.

## Select the saved results

Use one consistent experiment collection. Native `*_results.csv` files need
matching `*_config.rds` files. The historical `manifest.csv` layout also works.
`n` selects the sample size; `models` selects models. `lambda_settings: null`
uses all available settings; for example, `[[0.5, 0.5]]` selects one setting.

By default, `require_complete: true` requires a complete successful run.
Set it to `false` to retain converged rows with finite values for the selected
figures; `records/row_selection.csv` records every exclusion. Both histogram
methods always use the same replications. Only columns needed by `figure_types`
are required.

```{r setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = TRUE, warning = TRUE)
source("plot_individual.R")
if (!is.logical(params$run_plots) || length(params$run_plots) != 1L || is.na(params$run_plots))
  stop("run_plots must be TRUE or FALSE.")
```

## Export the figures

Existing output is preserved by creating `run_001`, `run_002`, etc. Set
`overwrite: true` only to replace matching files. Inputs are always read-only.
The returned folder contains PDFs, a gallery, input checksums, histogram bins,
and component summaries. The `latex/` folder retains the TeX sources.

```{r export}
if (isTRUE(params$run_plots)) {
  if (is.null(params$data_dir)) stop("Set data_dir to your saved results.")
  output <- gfm_plot_individual(
    data_dir = params$data_dir, output_dir = params$output_dir,
    n = params$n, models = params$models, lambda_settings = params$lambda_settings,
    histogram_bins = params$histogram_bins, figure_types = params$figure_types,
    overwrite = params$overwrite, previews = params$previews,
    require_complete = params$require_complete
  )
  knitr::kable(as.data.frame(table(output$figures$kind)),
               col.names = c("Figure type", "PDF count"))
  cat("Saved figures to:", output$output_dir, "\n")
} else {
  cat("Functions loaded. Set data_dir and run_plots: true to export figures.\n")
}
```

QQ plots use the saved standardized statistics without rescaling. Histograms
use the saved **unstandardized** `lambda_raw_error_*` and
`lambda_debiased_error_*` columns: diagonal entries are multiplied by
$\sqrt{2}$ to recover matrix units; off-diagonal entries are unchanged.
Adding the true entry gives the estimate. Matrix entries are in the saved
truth-aligned coordinate frame ($\Lambda_q$). The standardized `raw_lambda_*`
and `debiased_lambda_*` columns cannot replace these error columns.
